title: Claude Mythos Preview
content:
## Overview

Claude Mythos is Anthropic's most capable model — a full capability tier above Opus 4.7. Announced April 7, 2026, and currently in restricted preview under Project Glasswing, Anthropic has confirmed it plans to make Mythos available to all customers in the weeks following its May 2026 announcement alongside Opus 4.8.

Mythos stands out for two reasons: a generational jump in reasoning and software engineering benchmarks, and autonomous cybersecurity capabilities that sit at a threshold Anthropic's responsible scaling policy requires special handling for before broad deployment.

---

## Benchmarks

| Task | Opus 4.6 | Mythos Preview |
|---|---|---|
| USAMO 2026 | 42.3% | 97.6% |
| SWE-bench Verified | ~72% (est.) | 93.9% |
| SWE-bench Pro | — | 77.8% |
| Terminal-Bench 2.0 | — | 82.0% |

The USAMO gap (+55.3 percentage points) is, by Anthropic's framing, "a generational change" rather than an incremental improvement. SWE-bench Verified at 93.9% represents the highest publicly reported score on that benchmark as of May 2026.

---

## Cybersecurity Capabilities

Mythos is the first AI model to reach what the UK AI Security Institute classifies as expert-level autonomous offensive security capability:

- **73% success rate** on expert-level hacking tasks that no AI model could complete prior to April 2025, per UKASI evaluation.
- Autonomously identified and exploited a **17-year-old remote code execution vulnerability in FreeBSD** (CVE-2026-4747) — a privilege-escalation flaw exploitable by unauthenticated remote attackers with full root access.
- Has identified thousands of high-severity vulnerabilities spanning every major operating system and web browser.

These capabilities prompted Anthropic to restrict deployment: per its responsible scaling policy, models capable of autonomous expert-level exploitation require additional safeguards before broad public access.

---

## Project Glasswing

Access to Mythos Preview is restricted to approximately **fifty organizations** via Project Glasswing, which launched April 7, 2026, with twelve founding partners:

> Amazon, Apple, Broadcom, Cisco, CrowdStrike, Google, JPMorganChase, the Linux Foundation, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Palo Alto Networks, and Anthropic.

The program has since expanded to ~50 organizations that maintain critical software infrastructure. The design intent is to use Mythos for **defensive vulnerability research** — finding and patching flaws before adversaries exploit them — under controlled conditions with appropriate oversight.

---

## Deployment Timeline

As of late May 2026, Anthropic has publicly committed to a general release "in the coming weeks." Before broad availability, Anthropic intends to ship new safeguards with an updated Opus model — testing and refining those controls at lower risk before applying them to Mythos-level capability.

---

## Safety Framing

Mythos is the first Anthropic model released under an updated responsible scaling policy with explicit cybersecurity capability thresholds. Anthropic's transparency about the UKASI evaluation results, the CVE-2026-4747 discovery, and the Project Glasswing access restrictions represents a deliberate approach to communicating frontier-model risk publicly rather than discovering it after deployment.

The model's profile — exceptional at both legitimate software engineering and offensive security — illustrates why Anthropic frames the deployment question as one of *when* safeguards are mature enough, not *whether* to release.
